newsitem.title: FINLAND: HOUSEHOLDS' NEW FIM CREDITS HIT 36-MTH HIGH IN OCT.
newsitem.headline: HOUSEHOLDS' NEW FIM CREDITS HIT 36-MTH HIGH IN OCT.

text.p: New markka credits granted by banks to households rose further in October and exceeded four billion markka for the first time in three years, the Bank of Finland said in a monthly report received on Monday.

New markka credits granted to households in October totalled 4.05 billion markka -- the highest amount granted to households in any month since September 1993, the central bank said in its financial markets report 12/1996.
In September, banks granted new markka loans worth 3.76 billion to households, and this year's highest figure in any month so far had been 3.93 billion markka granted in May.

The stock of markka credits granted to households by Finnish banks rose for the fifth straight month, to 153.46 billion in October from 153.38 billion in September, but was still below the year-end level in excess of 155 billion markka.

The average rate of interest on new markka credits granted to households in October fell to 6.20 percent from 6.56 percent in September. At the turn of the year, the average interest rate on new markka loans to households was around 7.50 percent.
The average rate of interest on the stock of households' markka credits fell to 6.63 percent in October from 6.90 percent in September.

Finnish banks' extension of new markka credits to the corporate sector fell to 2.24 billion in October from 2.30 billion the month before. The average interest rate on new corporate markka credits edged up to 5.13 percent from 5.09 percent.

The stock of banks' markka credits to the corporate sector decreased for the fourth month in a row, to 82.46 billion in October from 82.56 billion in September. The average interest rate on the stock of corporate sector markka credits fell to 5.25 percent from 5.40 percent.

The stock of Finnish banks' total markka lending to the public stood at 270.10 billion markka at end-October, up from 269.47 billion a month earlier, with the average interest rate at 6.00 percent, down from 6.23 percent.
New markka credits granted by Finnish banks totalled 9.63 billion markka in October, down from 9.80 billion in September.
